messages:
jamie: heads up — multiple support tickets + synthetic alerts showing p99 latency jumping to ~45-60s for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Customers report timeouts. Any quick mitigations?

oncall-bot: ALERT: latency-p99 > 45s on route /v1/generate (us-west-2) — 12% error rate increase. Pager duty: oncall-eng paging jamie.

sara: @jamie thanks. first quick checks: any recent deploys in the last 30m? config changes to batching?

jamie: not from runtime team AFAIK. matt — did you kick any model or kernel changes?

matt: nope, no deploys. infra autoscaler did spin up a few nodes ~20m ago (normal), but GPU utilization on the serving pool is at 92% on some hosts.

kathy: can we immediately enable circuit-breaker -> fast-fail for requests above 10s to reduce queueing and lower backend load?

sara: +1. Also recommend immediate fallback routing to the smaller model variant for non-SLAs and add a temporary per-customer rate limit increase hold.

jamie: plan: 1) enable fast-fail circuit-breaker (10s) 2) route non-critical traffic to model-redwood-mini 3) apply soft rate-limits for heavy tenants 4) reduce batch size to 8 for that pool. executing now.

matt: i'm applying circuit-breaker policy via control-plane API. command:
```bash
# set cb to 10s fast-fail for pool 'gw-west-2'
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/policies/cb -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"pool":"gw-west-2","threshold_ms":10000,"mode":"fast-fail"}'
```

jinx: (automated) Policy update accepted. circuit-breaker active on gw-west-2.

sara: flipping routing for non-SLA customers to model-redwood-mini (fallback) using the routing policy: route_if CPU>80 OR p99>30s -> redwood-mini.

jamie: applying soft rate-limits to top 5 tenants contributing >40% of QPS: set per-tenant token bucket to 200r/s burst 400.

matt: lowering batch_size to 8 in the runtime config for the impacted pool now. snippet below:
```yaml
pool: gw-west-2
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch: 8
  max_latency_ms: 40
```

infra-bot: autoscaler: scaled +4 nodes to gw-west-2, starting. expected ready ~2m.

kathy: taking customer-facing action: posting to affected customers that we are actively mitigating and to retry in 2–3 minutes. cc @support.

sara: observed p99 dropped from 52s -> 18s after circuit-breaker + fallback, errors reduced to baseline. still watching.

jamie: next steps for full mitigation: 1) confirm if GPU OOMs or kernel stalls in the hot hosts 2) if model variant causes quality regression, rollback route for critical customers back to original model and throttle non-critical traffic 3) create short-lived SLA exemption for customers impacted by fallback so we don't penalize.

matt: pulling logs from 3 affected GPUs — seeing long tail due to KV cache thrashing when sequence lengths spike. suspects: rare job with 8k seq inputs. attaching sample log lines:
```
[2026-03-17T15:12:23Z] req_id=abc123 seq_len=8200 batch=1 latency_ms=48200 kernel_wait=47000
[2026-03-17T15:12:24Z] req_id=abc129 seq_len=120 batch=12 latency_ms=1200
```

sara: good catch. mitigation: add input-length guard to reject or pre-slice sequences >4k for the heavy path and send guidance to client SDK: return 413 + hint.

jamie: implemented pre-check hook to reject >4000 tokens for hosted path; config: 
```json
{"input_max_tokens":4000, "reject_code":413, "hint":"please truncate or use streaming chunked calls"}
```

kathy: reminder: also open a support play to chargeback heavy tenants if they repeatedly send >4k and cause disruptions.

sara: monitoring: p99 at 9s now, error rate back to normal. autoscale nodes are up; we'll keep cb + fallback for 10 more minutes, then slowly relax if stable.

jamie: postmortem owner assigned: @matt. please capture timeline + root cause (kv-cache thrash + long sequences) and follow-up actions: input-length enforcement, SDK updates, more aggressive per-tenant rate-limits, and a new circuit-breaker tuning doc.

matt: will do. quick action items for runbook updates: add explicit play for 'long sequence flood' w/ steps: 1) enable fast-fail cb 2) fallback model 3) apply input-length guard 4) throttle top tenants 5) scale pool. I'll add to runbook and ping for review.

kathy: thanks everyone. marking incident as mitigated but not closed. will keep thread open for 30m. :thumbsup:
